Azure Functions is a serverless solution that allows you to build robust apps while using less code, and with less infrastructure and lower costs. Instead of worrying about deploying and maintaining servers, you can use the cloud infrastructure to provide all the up-to-date resources needed to keep your applications running.
You focus on the code that matters most to you, in the most productive language for you, and Azure Functions handles the rest. For a list of supported languages, see [Supported languages in Azure Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/supported-languages).
## Scenarios
Functions provides a comprehensive set of event-driven [triggers and bindings](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-triggers-bindings) that connect your functions to other services without having to write extra code.
The following list includes common integrated scenarios that use Functions.
| If you want to... | then...| 
|  --- | ---  |
| [Process file uploads](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-scenarios#process-file-uploads) | Run code when a file is uploaded or changed in blob storage. |
| [Process data in real time](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-scenarios#real-time-stream-and-event-processing) | Capture and transform data from event and IoT source streams on the way to storage. |
| [Run AI inference](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-scenarios#machine-learning-and-ai) | Pull text from a queue and present it to various AI services for analysis and classification. |
| [Run scheduled task](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-scenarios#run-scheduled-tasks) | Execute data clean-up code on predefined timed intervals. |
| [Build a scalable web API](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-scenarios#build-a-scalable-web-api) | Implement a set of REST endpoints for your web applications using HTTP triggers. |
| [Build a serverless workflow](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-scenarios#build-a-serverless-workflow) | Create an event-driven workflow from a series of functions using Durable Functions. |
| [Respond to database changes](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-scenarios#respond-to-database-changes) | Run custom logic when a document is created or updated in a database. |
| [Create reliable message systems](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-scenarios#create-reliable-message-systems) | Process message queues using Azure Queue Storage, Service Bus, or Event Hubs. |

These scenarios allow you to build event-driven systems using modern architectural patterns. ## Overview
[Azure Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-overview) is a solution for easily running small pieces of code, or *functions*, in Azure. Azure Functions supports a [serverless](https://azure.microsoft.com/solutions/serverless/) execution model.
## Durable Functions extension
*Durable Functions* is an extension of [Azure Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-overview) that lets you write stateful functions in a serverless compute environment. The extension lets you define stateful workflows by writing [*orchestrator functions*](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/durable/durable-functions-orchestrations) and stateful entities by writing [*entity functions*](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/durable/durable-functions-entities) using the Azure Functions programming model. Behind the scenes, the extension manages state, checkpoints, and restarts for you, allowing you to focus on your business logic.
Install the extension [NuGet package](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Azure.WebJobs.Extensions.DurableTask) directly from the Visual Studio [Package Manager console](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/tools/package-manager-console) or with the [.NET Core CLI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/tools/dotnet-add-package).
The Azure API reference documentation supports [version 2.x of the Durable Functions extension](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/overview/azure/functions/runtime).
### Visual Studio package manager
```powershell
Install-Package Microsoft.Azure.WebJobs.Extensions.DurableTask
```
### .NET Core CLI
```dotnetcli
dotnet add package Microsoft.Azure.WebJobs.Extensions.DurableTask
```
### Getting started
## Samples

This article describes how to use either Azure Managed Redis or Azure Cache for Redis with Azure Functions to create optimized serverless and event-driven architectures.
Azure Functions provides an event-driven programming model where triggers and bindings are key features. With Azure Functions, you can easily build event-driven serverless applications. Azure Redis services (Azure Managed Redis and Azure Cache for Redis) provide a set of building blocks and best practices for building distributed applications, including microservices, state management, pub/sub messaging, and more.
Azure Redis can be used as a trigger for Azure Functions, allowing you to initiate a serverless workflow. This functionality can be highly useful in data architectures like a write-behind cache, or any event-based architectures.
You can integrate Azure Redis and Azure Functions to build functions that react to events from Azure Redis or external systems.
| Action | Direction| 
|  --- | ---  |
| [Trigger on Redis pub sub messages](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-cache-trigger-redispubsub) | Trigger |
| [Trigger on Redis lists](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-cache-trigger-redislist) | Trigger |
| [Trigger on Redis streams](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-cache-trigger-redisstream) | Trigger |
| [Read a cached value](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-cache-input) | Input |
| [Write a values to cache](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-cache-output) | Output |

## Scope of availability for functions triggers and bindings
| Tier | Azure Cache for Redis (Basic, Standard, Premium, Enterprise, Enterprise Flash) | Azure Managed Redis (Memory Optimized, Basic, Compute Optimized, Flash Optimized)|

| Pub/Sub | Yes | Yes |
| Lists | Yes | Yes |
| Streams | Yes | Yes |
| Bindings | Yes | Yes |

Azure Functions lets you implement your system's logic as event-driven, readily available blocks of code. These code blocks are called functions. Choose your preferred development language at the top of the article.
## Create your first function
Complete a quickstart article to create and deploy your first functions in less than five minutes.
You can create your first function by using one of the following tools:
1. [Azure Developer CLI (azd)](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/create-first-function-azure-developer-cli)
2. [Command line](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/how-to-create-function-azure-cli)

4. [Visual Studio](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-create-your-first-function-visual-studio)

# What is Azure Functions?
Azure Functions is a serverless solution that allows you to build robust apps while using less code, and with less infrastructure and lower costs. Instead of worrying about deploying and maintaining servers, you can use the cloud infrastructure to provide all the up-to-date resources needed to keep your applications running.
You focus on the code that matters most to you, in the most productive language for you, and Azure Functions handles the rest. For a list of supported languages, see [Supported languages in Azure Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/supported-languages).
## Scenarios
Functions provides a comprehensive set of event-driven [triggers and bindings](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-triggers-bindings) that connect your functions to other services without having to write extra code.
The following list includes common integrated scenarios that use Functions.
| If you want to... | then...| 
|  --- | ---  |
| [Process file uploads](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-scenarios#process-file-uploads) | Run code when a file is uploaded or changed in blob storage. |
| [Process data in real time](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-scenarios#real-time-stream-and-event-processing) | Capture and transform data from event and IoT source streams on the way to storage. |
| [Run AI inference](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-scenarios#machine-learning-and-ai) | Pull text from a queue and present it to various AI services for analysis and classification. |
| [Run scheduled task](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-scenarios#run-scheduled-tasks) | Execute data clean-up code on predefined timed intervals. |
| [Build a scalable web API](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-scenarios#build-a-scalable-web-api) | Implement a set of REST endpoints for your web applications using HTTP triggers. |
| [Build a serverless workflow](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-scenarios#build-a-serverless-workflow) | Create an event-driven workflow from a series of functions using Durable Functions. |

| [Create reliable message systems](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-scenarios#create-reliable-message-systems) | Process message queues using Azure Queue Storage, Service Bus, or Event Hubs. |

These scenarios allow you to build event-driven systems using modern architectural patterns. For more information, see [Azure Functions scenarios](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-scenarios).

results.content:
# Azure Functions libraries for .NET
## Overview
[Azure Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-overview) is a solution for easily running small pieces of code, or *functions*, in Azure. Azure Functions supports a [serverless](https://azure.microsoft.com/solutions/serverless/) execution model.
## Durable Functions extension
*Durable Functions* is an extension of [Azure Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-overview) that lets you write stateful functions in a serverless compute environment. The extension lets you define stateful workflows by writing [*orchestrator functions*](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/durable/durable-functions-orchestrations) and stateful entities by writing [*entity functions*](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/durable/durable-functions-entities) using the Azure Functions programming model. Behind the scenes, the extension manages state, checkpoints, and restarts for you, allowing you to focus on your business logic.
Install the extension [NuGet package](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Azure.WebJobs.Extensions.DurableTask) directly from the Visual Studio [Package Manager console](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/tools/package-manager-console) or with the [.NET Core CLI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/tools/dotnet-add-package).
The Azure API reference documentation supports [version 2.x of the Durable Functions extension](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/overview/azure/functions/runtime).
### Visual Studio package manager
```powershell
Install-Package Microsoft.Azure.WebJobs.Extensions.DurableTask
```
### .NET Core CLI
```dotnetcli
dotnet add package Microsoft.Azure.WebJobs.Extensions.DurableTask
```
### Getting started
## Samples
View the [complete list](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/samples/browse/?products=azure-functions&languages=csharp) of Azure Functions samples.

results.content:
# Overview of Azure functions for Azure Redis (programming-language-javascript)
This article describes how to use either Azure Managed Redis or Azure Cache for Redis with Azure Functions to create optimized serverless and event-driven architectures.
Azure Functions provides an event-driven programming model where triggers and bindings are key features. With Azure Functions, you can easily build event-driven serverless applications. Azure Redis services (Azure Managed Redis and Azure Cache for Redis) provide a set of building blocks and best practices for building distributed applications, including microservices, state management, pub/sub messaging, and more.
Azure Redis can be used as a trigger for Azure Functions, allowing you to initiate a serverless workflow. This functionality can be highly useful in data architectures like a write-behind cache, or any event-based architectures.
You can integrate Azure Redis and Azure Functions to build functions that react to events from Azure Redis or external systems.
| Action | Direction| 
|  --- | ---  |
| [Trigger on Redis pub sub messages](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-cache-trigger-redispubsub) | Trigger |
| [Trigger on Redis lists](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-cache-trigger-redislist) | Trigger |
| [Trigger on Redis streams](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-cache-trigger-redisstream) | Trigger |
| [Read a cached value](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-cache-input) | Input |
| [Write a values to cache](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-cache-output) | Output |

## Scope of availability for functions triggers and bindings
| Tier | Azure Cache for Redis (Basic, Standard, Premium, Enterprise, Enterprise Flash) | Azure Managed Redis (Memory Optimized, Basic, Compute Optimized, Flash Optimized)| 
|  --- | --- | ---  |
| Pub/Sub | Yes | Yes |
| Lists | Yes | Yes |
| Streams | Yes | Yes |
| Bindings | Yes | Yes |

Important
Redis triggers are currently only supported for functions running in either a [Elastic Premium plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-premium-plan) or a dedicated [App Service plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/dedicated-plan).

results.content:
# Get started with Azure Functions (programming-language-csharp)
Azure Functions lets you implement your system's logic as event-driven, readily available blocks of code. These code blocks are called functions. This article helps you find the most useful Azure Functions content quickly. For more general information about Azure Functions, see the [Introduction to Azure Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-overview).
Choose your preferred development language at the top of the article.
## Create your first function
Complete a quickstart article to create and deploy your first functions in less than five minutes.
You can create your first function by using one of the following tools:
1. [Azure Developer CLI (azd)](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/create-first-function-azure-developer-cli)
2. [Command line](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/how-to-create-function-azure-cli)
3. [Visual Studio Code](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/how-to-create-function-vs-code)
4. [Visual Studio](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-create-your-first-function-visual-studio)
## Review end-to-end samples
These sites let you browse existing functions reference projects and samples in your desired language:
1. [Awesome azd template library](https://azure.github.io/awesome-azd/?tags=functions&tags=dotnetCsharp)
2. [Azure Functions samples in GitHub](https://github.com/search?q=topic%3Aazure-functions+org%3AAzure-Samples+fork%3Atrue+language%3AC%23&type=repositories&l=C%23)
3. [Azure samples browser](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/samples/browse/?expanded=azure&languages=csharp&products=azure-functions)
## Scenarios
Here are some common scenarios to help you get started:
1. [Process file uploads](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-scenarios#process-file-uploads)
2. [Real-time stream and event processing](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-scenarios#real-time-stream-and-event-processing)
3. [Machine learning and AI](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-scenarios#machine-learning-and-ai)
4. [Run scheduled tasks](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-scenarios#run-scheduled-tasks)
5. [Build a scalable web API](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-scenarios#build-a-scalable-web-api)
6. [Build a serverless workflow](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-scenarios#build-a-serverless-workflow)
7. [Respond to database changes](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-scenarios#respond-to-database-changes)
8. [Create reliable message systems](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-scenarios#create-reliable-message-systems)
